V09 took neither: §4.21.13 (1) (l. 3678–3680) 'an element shows damaged while the building's decay level is above 0 and at least its threshold t'; §4.21.13 (2) (l. 3698–3699) 'an element the plan gained after its damage left is drawn as built'; row 92 (l. 1612) the same. For a `reoccupy` whose re-cut is made while its `repair` Works runs, V09's gloss draws the minted partitions, doors and furniture damaged where V03, V06, §2.6 and V10 draw them as built. V09's lines are V03's damage layer (§1b l. 378; §2.12 l. 1010), so nothing built changes; only V09's gloss is narrower. It is VDC4-01's omission (§6.3) at V09, one fix with it.

claim: Under R4-02 the view draws its working layer whatever that layer's `LayerSpec.visible` (base §8.4 l. 13580-13585; §2.9 l. 3396; V09 §4.2 l. 1652-1656). So the per-viewer key `workingLayer` (V09 §2.4: `{ layer: 'sky'; key: PlatKey }` names one island) now decides what the view draws, what §8.8's tiles key on, and which arena every tool acts on (V09 §4.20.9: 'the chosen island's arena with its `key`'). No text says what happens when that value names something the document no longer holds. Ordinary edits cause it: a user on Sky creates an island (T5 `quarter` with `sky`) and undoes it; deletes the island; an epoch's landfall drops it (row 80 gives the remains to Ground but says nothing of the working layer); T1 `intend` turns the islands setting off; Below's last tunnel, cavern or ruin is undone. V09 §3.16 row 21 (l. 1526) disables the Sky and Below switches 'at a rung without islands' and 'with no network', which is the switch's state at rest, not its current value. §2.12's row (l. 974) reads 'an unknown value' as `ground`, and a well-formed key of a removed island is no unknown value. Builders would reset to Ground, keep Sky drawing nothing with every tool's dry run refused on a dangling key, or crash on the missing arena. A redo, and a load of a document whose saved view names the island, raise the same question. This is an edge on a normal path (an undo on the working layer) with no defined outcome.
required_change: 1. V09 §4.2, after 'a layer's own visibility is §7.8's layer controls, T12 `dress`'s logged `setLayer`.', add: 'A working layer naming what the document no longer holds — Sky with an island `key` no standing island carries (its creation undone, the island deleted or fallen in a landfall, the islands setting off) or Below with no network, cavern or ruin left — reads as Ground: at the `doc.changed` that removes it, and at a load, the view key becomes `{ layer: 'ground' }` (a view key, nothing written, no event), the switch shows Ground with Sky or Below disabled by its reason, and a draft on that layer re-previews and is refused as any draft whose target is gone; a redo that restores the island leaves the working layer Ground. At a drawn week whose frame lacks the island the key stands and the view draws the frame's layers (§8.4).' 2. V09 §2.12's `workingLayer` row, last cell, add '; a Sky key no standing island carries, or Below with no network, cavern or ruin, reads `ground` (V09 §4.2)'. 3. V09 §3.16 row 21 adds the edge 'the working layer's island, or Below's last network, cavern or ruin, removed while it is the working layer (an undo, a delete, a landfall, the islands setting off)' with the outcome 'the working layer Ground, nothing written, the switch disabled with its reason (V09 §4.2)'. 4. T-V9-80 (21) adds: 'Sky the working layer on an island just created, its creation undone: the working layer Ground, 0 events logged, the Sky switch disabled with its reason, a redo leaving it Ground; a document saved with Sky on an island since deleted, reloaded: Ground'.

claim: V09 §4.21.9 (1) (l. 3431–3434) was written in round 4 from VV56-r3-02's required text (this verifier's). It reads 'but a dossier catch-up whose events' absorb term passes its budget, which folds one epoch over the span and completes past it'. That is the events-alone trigger VV56-r3-01 removed from V06's five summaries. Its home, V06 §6.8 (6), and V06 §1.1 (14), W91, §6.8's lead and (3), §3.21's dossier-bound row, T-V6-24, J-V6.136 and V08 §3.6 (3) all state the trigger as 'where even one epoch over the span with its (dossier) events' (absorb) term passes the budget'. The two differ when the events' term (now V08 §6's batch: b per epoch folded plus a per event) is under the budget but one epoch plus it is over. At the metropolis cap with three islands and the hand-placed cap, inside an open, one epoch with its batch cost is ≈ 5.8 s of 6 310 ms, so about 150 events at 3.5 ms reach the branch while the events' term alone is about 1 s. The progress view is 'unchanged' either way, so nothing built changes.
required_change: In V09 §4.21.9 (1), replace 'but a dossier catch-up whose events' absorb term passes its budget, which folds one epoch over the span and completes past it' with 'but a dossier catch-up where even one epoch over the span with its dossier events' absorb term passes its budget, which folds that one epoch and completes past it'. The rest of the sentence stays as it is.

claim: V09 §4.9's `info.crisis.<line>` row (l. 2192) gives the why line four forms — `line`, `lineOpen` (no `untilWeek`), `lineUnnamed` (no `name`), `preview` — and `ruinedFor` one: "For now: {look}, {condition}, weeks {a}–{b}". Round 4's §4.21.12 (4) (l. 3624–3634) gives `ruinedFor` as the why card's `facts` row to every building a disaster look stands over, "under a preview … every building of the preview's units", and §4.21.13 (3) (l. 3700–3705) makes it the plan panel's head there ("its words from the look's entry … or the preview's"); row 92 and T-V9-86 add "under a `disaster` preview the look". A preview's entry has no condition, name or weeks (§11.2's `LooksAnswer.crises[]`: `condition?` "absent on a preview", `sinceWeek?`, `untilWeek?`, l. 16321–16322; V10 §3.9b (8): "no condition, name, source or weeks"), so on the standalone preview — "the only way to see a look on a map without a dossier" (§4.21.12 (2)) — the row's slots have no values. A standing look with no `untilWeek` (row 90's open condition) or no `name` meets the same one form, and the why line itself has no form for a look with neither (`lineOpen` needs `{condition}`, `lineUnnamed` needs `{b}`); V10 §2.13's `says` (l. 1013) lists the same four keys. Two builders render different words, or fail on a missing slot, on a common path.

claim: V09 §4.21.12 (4) (l. 3624–3625) and §5.8 (l. 3992–3993) give `info.crisis.ruinedFor` to the why card "of a field a famine leaves bare". A famine bares a share of the `fields` place's faces — round(s × n) of them, by keyed draws on the render keys from the seed and the condition's id (§10.2 (c) l. 15630–15635, (d) l. 15642 and 15682, (f) l. 15710–15711) — so whether one field is bare is the generation worker's evaluation. Round 4 gave V09 that evaluation for a disaster's buildings (§11.2's `looks` asked with `building`, each `disaster` entry's `over`; R4-04 (c)) and none for a field: `building?` and `over` are defined for a building and a disaster look only (base l. 16280, 16325), and V09 may not run the placement on the main thread. So the card's famine row reads an input nothing produces: one builder shows it on every field while a famine stands, another on none, and no edge row or bar covers it (row 90, T-V9-85). (At THORP, HAMLET and VILLAGE a `VillageField`'s row is V07's provider's, R3-16 (e); this is the town ladder's field.)
